key_insight: Use reinforcement learning at test time to let an LLM continue training on the specific problem instance, optimizing for one exceptional solution rather than average-case performance — enabling discovery of new state-of-the-art outcomes for scientific tasks.
problem_solved: Prior test-time scaling methods (e.g., prompting a frozen LLM) search without model adaptation and optimize average performance; this paper addresses how to adapt a model at test time to produce a single best solution tailored to the specific test problem.
method: Run reinforcement learning updates at test time so the model learns from instance-specific feedback (episodic test-time fine-tuning).
Design a reward and exploration strategy that prioritizes finding one high-quality solution rather than improving expected / average metrics.
Compare and contrast with frozen-prompt search (e.g., AlphaEvolve) to demonstrate gains from continuing to train the model during evaluation.
impact: Enables practitioners and researchers to push state-of-the-art on individual scientific problems by adapting models during evaluation, making automated discovery and problem-specific optimization more effective; practical adoption will require careful reward design and compute budgeting.
visual_elements: Flowchart of the test-time RL loop: input instance → LLM policy → candidate solution → reward signal → policy update
Two-panel performance graphic: frozen-prompt search (many decent solutions) vs test-time RL (one superior solution) highlighting max vs mean performance
Comparison diagram showing frozen prompting pipeline vs continual test-time training pipeline
Icon set: reward cup (single best), stopwatch/compute meter (test-time cost), target icon (instance-specific optimization)
paper_title: Learning to Discover at Test Time
paper_authors: Mert Yuksekgonul, Daniel Koceja, Xinhao Li, Federico Bianchi, Jed McCaleb
